name: Supersequence
description: An array $$$a$$$ is called a subsequence of an array $$$b$$$ if some elements can be removed from array $$$b$$$ (possibly all, possibly none) to obtain the array $$$a$$$. You are given an array $$$a = [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n]$$$. We call an array $$$b = [b_1, b_2, \dots, b_m]$$$ beautiful if: $$$a$$$ is a subsequence of $$$b$$$; for each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$m-1$$$, the elements $$$b_i$$$ and $$$b_{i+1}$$$ differ by exactly $$$1$$$ (that is, $$$|b_i - b_{i+1}| = 1$$$); among all arrays that satisfy these two requirements, the length of $$$b$$$ is minimum. You have to process $$$q$$$ queries. In the $$$i$$$-th query, a single integer $$$x_i$$$ is given. Your task is as follows: if $$$x_i$$$ is greater than the minimum possible number of elements in a beautiful array, print $$$-1$$$; otherwise, if the same number occupies position $$$x_i$$$ in all beautiful arrays, print that number; otherwise, print $$$0$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). The third line contains $$$q$$$ integers $$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_q$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i \le 10^{18}$$$).
output_specification: For each query, print a single integer — the answer to it.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2199E — Supersequence [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
